content.comment_body: Just installed [version_no] and noticed odd scaling and font issues in the GUI compared to [version_no] :-(
The changes in fonts and scaling are aimed at users with high-resolution monitors. For standard resolutions like 1920x1200, the fonts in [product_name] [version_no] were preferable.
Honestly, I'm glad for the updates, as I've struggled with eye strain at 3200x1800 resolution in [product_name] [version_no].

I agree with [user_name]. Condensed fonts do not improve readability on high-resolution screens – I'm using 2560x1080 and find the new font less effective. The updated ability to scale text and icons helps laptop users, but there should be more scaling steps. The choice of condensed font seems questionable. I also wonder why [product_name] doesn’t utilize Windows built-in accessibility scaling.

It's surprising that such a large company would release software with such an unimpressive GUI. The condensed font causes real discomfort. It feels unfinished, like a beta version seeking feedback. Sadly, these issues might linger for a long time.

analysis.insight_summary: Users observed noticeable changes in scaling and fonts in [product_name] [version_no] compared to previous versions. Although updates are intended to improve usability on high-resolution screens, many users report increased eye strain and consider the condensed font a drawback. While scaling options are welcome, users remain dissatisfied with font readability and the lack of integration with system-level accessibility adjustments.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect upgrades to maintain or enhance readability and comfort, and would like the software to better utilize native accessibility and scaling features offered by the operating system.
